reviewer: u2b-A — adversarial refutation pass, blind to the second reviewer

flags.detail: The question pins itself to 'the OWASP Top 10 (2021 edition)' and keys SSRF as A10, which was correct for 2021. But the OWASP Top 10:2025 was published 6 Nov 2025 and finalised in January 2026 — it is the current list as of this user's 2026 exam, and it deleted SSRF as a standalone category and folded CWE-918 into A01:2025 Broken Access Control (confirmed at https://owasp.org/Top10/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/, which names CWE-918 among its notable CWEs). The specific fact this question tests is therefore precisely the fact that has since been reversed, and the option it teaches the student to reject — 'Broken Access Control' — is the option that is now correct. Edition-pinning makes the question internally consistent but does not make it safe to drill: a student who memorises 'SSRF = A10, not Broken Access Control' will answer a 2026 exam wrongly. Fix: re-key to the 2025 taxonomy (stem 'In the OWASP Top 10 (2025 edition)', key A01:2025 Broken Access Control, with A10:2025 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions and A03:2025 Software Supply Chain Failures as fresh distractors), or drop the numbering and ask the concept. Note the 2025 renumbering also moves Injection to A05, Cryptographic Failures to A04 and Security Misconfiguration to A02, so any distractor set carried over from the 2021 list needs rebuilding, not just relabelling.
flags.suggested: A — but only after restating the stem as the 2025 edition and rebuilding the distractors to 2025 category names/numbers.

flags.detail: Two separate problems. (1) The stem names a real package — lodash — and then asks 'which of these published versions may npm install resolve the dependency to?', but the keyed answer 4.19.3 has never been published (https://registry.npmjs.org/lodash/4.19.3 returns 404; the registry's dist-tags.latest is 4.18.1). 5.0.1 has never been published either. So the assertion 'these published versions' is false of the key itself, and a candidate who actually knows lodash's release history — exactly the practitioner the paper is aimed at — finds that the only in-range option does not exist and has no defensible answer. The semver reasoning being tested is sound; the fix is to strip the false factual claim, either by using a fictional package name ('"acme-utils": "^4.17.20"') or by rewording to 'which of these version numbers falls inside the range'. (2) Leaf mismatch: this question is filed under sub 'Architecture and scale: MVC, microservices, SOLID, event-driven systems, caching and queues', but npm caret-range resolution is not architecture-and-scale material and has no architectural framing in the stem — unlike GEN-T2U2-080 and GEN-T2U2-086, which are Nginx/Kubernetes questions deliberately framed onto their AI leaf. As filed it makes the Architecture unit drill package-manager trivia. Move it to the Git/Docker/CI-CD/deployment leaf, or replace it with an architecture question.
flags.suggested: Keep key B, but change the package to a fictional name (or reword to 'which of these version numbers satisfies the range'), and re-file under the 'Git version control, Docker, CI/CD, Linux administration, Nginx and deployment' leaf.

notes: Genuinely strong batch — I attacked all 45 for wrong keys, accidentally-true distractors and unstated assumptions and could not break the other 43. I specifically verified against sources the claims most likely to be fabricated: CERT-In's 28 Apr 2022 six-hour reporting window and 180-day Indian log retention (GEN-T2U2-087, correct), MCP's use of JSON-RPC 2.0 and its resources/tools/prompts primitives, which survive unchanged into the current 2026-07-28 spec revision (GEN-T2U2-081/082, not stale), RFC 6750's insufficient_scope-to-403 mapping (047), RFC 9110's If-Match-to-412 rule (051), and lodash's actual published version list (079). The recurring design of stems that use a superlative to exclude a genuinely-good-practice distractor — 'most directly eliminates' in 058, 'specifically intended to stop this propagation' in 074, 'a user who has never visited the site before' in 065, 'actually addresses' in 088 — does real work each time and I judged none of them ambiguous; the one place that discipline slipped is 063, where the edition-pin is honest but the pinned edition is now superseded.
